THE SANCTIONED equivalent_copy_form CLASS IS DIRECTIONAL, AND ITS INVERSE DIRECTION — OURS IS THE COPY, THE TARGET IS THE `li` — HAS NO PROOF MODE AT ALL. This is a boundary on claim.LZ_webfrank-equivalent-copy-form-edit-class.20260901.v1, which is correct in everything it states but describes its two proof modes from one side only and never says the class is asymmetric. Both shipped modes require the TARGET word to decode as a register copy: `unconditional` (both sides copy rD<-rS, rS!=0) and `dominating_def` / `dominating_def_across_calls` (ours `li rD,K`, target a copy). MEASURED REFUSAL on the inverse: dcsHandleRequest +0x1e0, ours `addi r30,r31,0` (a copy) against target `li r28,0`, is refused with '+0x1e0: target word 0x3b800000 is not a register copy' — refused positionally AND after a hypothetical permutation that aligns the words. THIS DIRECTION IS NOT RARE: the LZ census's own form-pair table lists `addi_copy->li 5` and `mr->li 1`, i.e. six image-wide sites, alongside the 12+5 it does serve. Anyone triaging a residual by the LZ taxonomy must read the arrow, not just the pair: half the census rows name a population the rule cannot touch. Do not spend a derivation discovering this per function.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT BAR, WORTH ITS OWN LINE BECAUSE IT DEFEATS dominating_def WHEREVER A SWITCH IS PRESENT: A CANDIDATE SITE THAT IS A JUMPTABLE CASE-ENTRY CAN NEVER CARRY A dominating_def PROOF. prove_constant_source fails closed on the first index reachable by anything but its own fallthrough edge, and `_jumptable_targets` correctly makes every switch case label such an index. On dcsHandleRequest the candidate site +0x1e0 IS one of the 19 jumptable targets, so the backward scan is barred before it starts. This is the MtapOpenPort refusal generalised from a `bne` target to a switch arm, and it means the li-variant payoff set — the whole value of the class per the LZ payoff inversion — systematically EXCLUDES the first instruction of any switch arm. Screen for it with one call to `_jumptable_targets` before attempting a proof.

THIRD, THE COMPOSITION ORDER READ FROM THE SOURCE, which decides whether a form fix can rescue an illegal permutation: apply_patch runs instruction_permutation -> permute_instruction_atoms -> equivalent_copy_form -> copy_register_fields -> verify_consistent_recolor. THE FORM STAGE RUNS AFTER THE PERMUTATION, NEVER BEFORE IT. This matters because a copy word creates a def-use edge that a `li` does not: on dcsHandleRequest the permutation is refused with 'breaks def-use chains: [(1, (g,31))]' precisely because our `addi r30,r31,0` reads the r31 that our `li r31,0` defines, whereas the target's independent `li r28,0` reads nothing. Rewriting the form FIRST would dissolve that edge and make the reorder legal — but the stage that would do it runs third. So the C1 law's step-0 membership test is evaluated against a colouring AND a form the later stages will change, and a function can be a C1 non-member SOLELY because of a copy form that a reordered pipeline would have removed. STATE THIS WHEN RECORDING A C1 NON-MEMBER: distinguish 'the displacement is caused by the register assignment' (genuinely unreachable, the sceOpen case) from 'the displacement is caused by a copy FORM the pipeline fixes too late' (this case), because only the second is unblocked by a pipeline change.

CONSEQUENCE, and the concrete v2 shape this evidence supports: dcsHandleRequest needs form + permute + recolor at ONE three-word site, and is barred FOUR times over — inverse direction, jumptable case-entry, differing destination registers (the camera_mode_level 'v2 requirement' already on record), and step-0 illegality that is itself an artifact of the stage order. A v2 combined pass would need to admit the inverse direction, evaluate permutation legality AFTER the form rewrite, and adjudicate renaming and form together. Until such a pass exists, treat any residual whose window mixes a copy-form word with a reorder as STRUCTURALLY CLOSED to WebFrank and record it as source-exhausted rather than as a candidate.
